the bond strength of dental porcelain to titanium based alloys was reduced after thermal and mechanical fatigue, while the bond strength of porcelain to cobalt chromium alloy was not affected.
the porcelain bond strength to titanium based alloys is affected not only by the applied processing technology, but also by the thermo mechanical cycling.

the shear bond strength of porcelain to Co Cr based dental alloys is not reduced by thermal and mechanical fatigue while porcelain bond strength to titanium dental alloys is affected by thermo mechanical cycling and the applied fabrication method of the titanium alloy.

the effect of thermo-mechanical fatigue on the bond strength of dental porcelain to metal alloys, and with the role of the metal processing technology on this bond strength.
the influence of the metal processing technology and the effect of thermo-mechanical fatigue on the porcelain bond strength of Co Cr and Ti-based alloys.
the influence of thermo mechanical cycling and metal processing on the porcelain bond strength to dental alloys.

the SLM fabricated Ti 6Al4V alloy is the most susceptible to reduction in bond strength following thermo-mechanical fatigue.
